more.title: How psychopathic traits shape language
more.summary: Popular culture often depicts people with psychopathy as cold, emotionless and hollow, but a recent University of Mississippi study found that the language associated with psychopathic traits is more complicated than often described.

more.title: Rare insect discovery reveals a new species from the dinosaur age
more.summary: Some 99 million years ago, during the age of the dinosaurs, a tiny insect belonging to a species previously unknown to science became trapped in tree resin. The resin hardened and turned into amber, and the fossil preserved within it has now enabled a team of researchers from the School of Zoology and The Steinhardt Museum of Natural History to identify and describe a new species: Cretodorus noonoo, or "Noo-Noo."

more.title: Switching on brain cells: The Nobel-winning science of optogenetics
more.summary: In optogenetics, scientists control neurons by stimulating them with light—potentially unlocking breakthroughs for conditions such as dementia, depression and blindness.

more.title: California scientist wins a Nobel Prize, then makes school lunches for his kids
more.summary: Dr. Karl Deisseroth spent hours fielding congratulatory calls after learning early Monday that he had won a Nobel Prize for medicine for helping to open a new field of brain science called optogenetics.

NASA’s engagement at NFL games is […]

more.title: Standard 3D printers let labs build and adapt tools for bacterial research
more.summary: Studying microorganisms requires instruments with extremely high precision. Such instruments are expensive and take a long time to manufacture using traditional methods, which has slowed progress in the field. It has also been difficult for the biologists who use these instruments to participate directly in their development.

more.title: How game publishers set international prices: A study reveals four pricing approaches on Steam
more.summary: Although digital platforms make it possible to sell the same product globally, prices often vary across countries because of differences in purchasing power, currencies, taxation and other market conditions. At the same time, the transparency of online prices enables consumers to compare prices across regions easily.

more.title: NASA Testing Aims at Supercooled Large Droplet Aviation Safety
more.author: Dede Dinius
more.summary: NASA is leveraging its expertise and enhancing its test facilities to help address a rare but persistent aviation hazard: icing that occurs when aircraft encounter unusually large, very cold water droplets in clouds. The problem, known as “supercooled large droplet icing,” occurs when aircraft fly through clouds containing unusually large drops of water that are […]

more.title: Suspected Second-generation Planet Solves NASA Hubble Cold Case
more.summary: New analysis of archival Hubble data points to the possibility of “dead” white dwarf stars hosting second-generation planetary systems.

more.author: Palak Sharma
more.summary: Smart kitchen brand Beyond Appliances has raised ₹110 Cr ($10.4 Mn) in a Series B funding round led by Fireside…

more.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
more.author: Jordana Cepelewicz
more.summary: Mathematicians are facing the sudden shift with grief, anger, and a desperate search for fresh ideas: “If we don’t adapt, there’s just no more math in 50 years.” The post Is AI the End of Math As We Know It? first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: 5 startups that caught VCs’ attention at the latest PearX demo day
more.author: Marina Temkin
more.summary: TechCrunch attended Pear’s latest demo day and discovered which startups generated the most buzz, from spatial models to chips for local AI.

more.title: Exploring systemic racism as the default explanation for disparities
more.summary: Much of the field of sociology treats systemic racism as its default explanation for racial disparities rather than as an open question that requires further investigation and evidence, according to a recent position paper. The assumptions and moralization surrounding the origins of race-based disparities have undermined the discipline and made it difficult—and professionally costly—to challenge the concept, says…

more.title: Vitamin B1 gains in wild lake trout embryos challenge assumptions drawn from hatcheries
more.summary: For decades, fisheries managers have struggled to restore recruitment in wild lake trout populations across the Great Lakes region, with limited success. Returning this species to its former abundance is hampered by overfishing, sea lamprey predation, invasive species and habitat alterations.

more.title: Global review reveals major blind spots in our understanding of climate change impacts on Mediterranean ecosystems
more.summary: A new global review of observed climate change impacts on plant communities reveals major gaps in where and how we monitor some of the world's most climate-vulnerable ecosystems.

more.title: Neutrons, rotating black holes, and a galactic PeVatron at the center of the Milky Way
more.summary: Galactic black holes are cosmic mitochondria, powerhouses of the universe. Most of the energy these supermassive black holes produce comes from the material surrounding them: superheated plasma in their accretion disks interacting with tremendous magnetic fields. But there is a more direct way to extract energy from a black hole.

more.title: Why some Indigenous communities don't resist oil extraction in their territories
more.summary: More than half of the Ecuadorian Amazon has been marked for oil drilling, overlapping with Indigenous territories and areas of high biodiversity. The ecological and cultural impacts of oil extraction are well documented and have fueled some of Latin America's most prominent environmental movements. Yet at the local level, extraction is not always met with resistance.

more.title: Global soil erosion outpaces natural recovery, report warns
more.summary: Isaac Larsen, an associate professor in the College of Natural Sciences' Department of Earth, Geographic, and Climate Sciences, is a lead author of "Status of the World's Soil Resources 2026," a new report produced by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) that draws on recent scientific literature and contributions from hundreds of experts around the world.

more.title: Scientists discover a human brain gene that can jump through DNA
more.summary: Scientists have discovered a human gene with a remarkable double life: it appears to play an important role in brain cells while still retaining the ability to jump around the genome. Called BC200, the gene evolved millions of years ago from a mobile piece of DNA known as a transposon, but unlike most genes that arose this way, it never lost its mobility.

more.title: Game simulator shows how math can guide decisions when resources are limited
more.summary: In "Bloons Tower Defense," the goal is to stop balloons from reaching the end of a track by strategically placing towers along the route. These towers vary in cost, range and attack power, and they also take up valuable space. The game becomes increasingly difficult with each round. Where you place a tower therefore determines not only how effective it is now but also which options remain available later in the game.

more.title: 'Digital ibuprofen' offers Chinese youth comfort through cute characters facing familiar struggles
more.summary: In China, young people are encountering a myriad of challenges, from societal pressures around success to life in a highly surveilled society, that have led them to turn to the internet in search of a balm to soothe their pain. What has emerged is a host of content called "digital ibuprofen"—viewed as a way to numb the anxieties of modern living.

more.title: This hidden device could free up gigawatts of power for the US grid
more.author: Maria Gallucci
more.summary: America’s energy supply crunch is driving a surge of federal and private investment in new electricity generation — from polluting gas turbines to cleaner developments like solar farms and geothermal plants. But gigawatts of power are already available for the taking across the U.S. economy in the form of wasted…

more.title: Attention can't be bought, so brands turn to memes
more.summary: The funniest post you saw this week may not have come from a friend; it may have come from a brand. Whether it is Kohl's, Wendy's, or Netflix, brands are behaving more like internet users than traditional advertisers.
